rationale: This is a one-term cosmetic variant of the archive's best signal (Cash-Backed Profit Floor), swapping `che` for `che-dlc` — a numerator already used in Liquidity-Backed Intangible Productivity — so it tests no new mechanism and risks appearing to "improve" on noise.

The valuation leg is identical to the archive's strongest signal, but replacing the temporal profitability floor with a cross-sectional MIN over accrual and cash ROA is a substantively different gating mechanism (does cash-richness need persistence or dual-channel confirmation?) that is worth one test.

Coherent and internally consistent combination of R&D-capitalized ROIC with a three-year floor and cash-flow yield, though it sits close to two archive signals and inherits their ~9% coverage from `oancf`, so the incremental information is modest.

This is a mechanical splice of two existing archive signals (the ni-yield × drawdown-penalized-profitability structure and the fixed-charge coverage ratio) with the added flaw that a drawdown penalty on an unbounded, explosive coverage ratio (xint+dp → 0) is not on a comparable scale to the level term it is subtracted from.

Genuinely new theme for this archive with a clean economic story (payout sustainability net of asset maintenance) and consistent expected sign, though dividend yield itself is a long-published anomaly and the mass of zero-dividend firms plus a possibly near-zero `dvc+dp` denominator will need diagnostic attention.

The oiadp/xsga overhead-productivity leg is a genuinely different quality construct from the archive's SG&A-trend and margin-recovery variants and is motivated by a specific diagnosis of the prior sales-to-EV alpha reversal, but the ratio is unstable for low-SG&A and loss-making firms and reliability of the mean-minus-vol transform on such a ratio is questionable.
